title: Group portrait of the VLT with laser beam
caption: The Very Large Telescope with a laser beam under star trails, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Stars have traced circular trails across a dark, clear sky over Cerro Paranal, and among them a laser beam shoots up from one of the Unit Telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope. ESO describes the VLT as the most advanced observatory in the world.
The beam creates an artificial star high above Paranal. That fake star is a reference point for the VLT's adaptive optics instruments.

Adaptive optics tackles a basic problem of ground-based astronomy. Earth's atmosphere is constantly moving, and it blurs the light of stars before it reaches the telescope. By watching how the artificial star twinkles and wobbles, the system can measure that blurring and correct for it on the fly. The result, according to ESO, is images almost as sharp as the telescope could deliver if it were in space, above the atmosphere entirely.

understand.summary: This is a long-exposure landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at Paranal. The exposure settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye would see the stars as points. The circular trails appear only because the camera collected light over a long time.

explore: The circular star trails come from Earth's rotation during a long exposure, as the sky appears to pivot around the celestial pole, and each star draws an arc. The laser cuts straight through them.
alt: Circular star trails in a dark sky above telescope enclosures, with a laser beam shooting up from one of them.
